chunks: "Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, did not create a spot on earth more beloved to Him than it"—and he gestured with his hand toward the Kaaba
"nor more honored by Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than it. For its sake, Allah (swt) sanctified the sacred months in His Book"
"on the day He created the heavens and the earth."

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Kaaba, the sacred house in Mecca
key_terms.يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ: On the day He created the heavens and the earth

ai.seo_question: Why is the Kaaba considered the most beloved place to Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq emphasizes the Kaaba's primordial status as the most beloved and honored locus on earth, linking its sanctity to the divine consecration of the sacred months. The reference to 'the day He created the heavens and the earth' underscores the eternal nature of this honor, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the Kaaba's sanctity is rooted in the very act of creation, serving as a focal point for spiritual orientation (Qibla) and divine proximity.
